content.text:
Here’s a **first-timer-friendly 7-day China itinerary** that balances imperial history, food, scenery, and modern city life:

## Best 7-day route: **Beijing → Xi’an → Shanghai**

This is the classic “China highlights” route: **Great Wall + Forbidden City + Terracotta Warriors + Shanghai skyline**, using high-speed rail or short flights between cities.

> **Entry note:** If you’re traveling on a U.S. passport, you may need either a tourist visa or to structure the trip as eligible visa-free transit, depending on your route and current rules. China has expanded a **240-hour/10-day visa-free transit** option for eligible nationalities, but it generally requires confirmed onward travel to a third country/region, not a simple U.S.–China–U.S. round trip. Verify before booking. ([mychina.guide](https://mychina.guide/blog/china-visa-free-transit-requirements?utm_source=openai))

---

# Day 1 — Arrive in Beijing

**Base:** Beijing  
**Plan:**
- Arrive, check into a hotel in **Dongcheng** or **Wangfujing** for easy sightseeing.
- Light evening walk around:
  - **Wangfujing**
  - **Qianmen Street**
  - Optional: view **Tiananmen Square** area by night

**Food to try:** Peking duck, zhajiangmian, jianbing.

**Tip:** Don’t overload Day 1—international arrivals plus immigration and transport can be tiring.

---

# Day 2 — Forbidden City, Tiananmen & old Beijing

**Base:** Beijing  
**Morning:**
- **Tiananmen Square**
- **Forbidden City**

**Afternoon:**
- **Jingshan Park** for the best overhead view of the Forbidden City
- Explore the **hutongs** around Shichahai or Nanluoguxiang

**Evening:**
- Dinner near **Houhai** or **Gulou**

**Tip:** Book major Beijing attractions in advance where possible, and bring your passport, as many attractions and trains use real-name ID checks.

---

# Day 3 — Great Wall day trip

**Base:** Beijing  
**Best section:** **Mutianyu Great Wall**  
It’s scenic, restored, and usually easier for first-time visitors than Badaling.

**Plan:**
- Morning departure from Beijing
- Visit **Mutianyu Great Wall**
- Optional cable car/chairlift up, toboggan/cable car down
- Return to Beijing by late afternoon

**Evening:**
- Peking duck dinner or casual hotpot

**Alternative:** If you’re very fit and want a wilder experience, consider **Jinshanling**, but it’s farther away.

---

# Day 4 — Beijing to Xi’an

**Base:** Xi’an  
**Transport:** High-speed train from Beijing to Xi’an, usually around **4.5–6 hours**, depending on service.

Foreign travelers can generally book high-speed rail using a passport through the official 12306 platform, Trip.com/Ctrip, or station ticket windows; bring the same passport used for booking when entering the station and boarding. ([chinatravelplus.com](https://www.chinatravelplus.com/f755376/How-to-Buy-High-Speed-Train-Tickets-in-China-as-a-Foreigner-Complete-Guide-2026.htm?utm_source=openai))

**Afternoon/evening in Xi’an:**
- Check into hotel near the **Bell Tower** or **South Gate**
- Walk or cycle part of the **Xi’an City Wall**
- Dinner in the **Muslim Quarter**

**Food to try:** Roujiamo, biangbiang noodles, lamb skewers, yangrou paomo.

---

# Day 5 — Terracotta Warriors & Xi’an

**Base:** Xi’an  
**Morning:**
- Visit the **Terracotta Warriors**
- Consider hiring a guide; the site is much more meaningful with historical context.

**Afternoon:**
- Optional visit to:
  - **Big Wild Goose Pagoda**
  - **Shaanxi History Museum**
  - **Great Mosque**
  - **City Wall** if you didn’t do it the day before

**Evening:**
- Tang-style performance or food tour

---

# Day 6 — Xi’an to Shanghai

**Base:** Shanghai  
**Transport options:**
- **Flight:** fastest and usually easiest
- **High-speed train:** possible, but longer — often about 6–7+ hours

**Afternoon/evening in Shanghai:**
- Check into hotel around **People’s Square**, **Nanjing Road**, **Jing’an**, or **The Bund**
- Walk along **The Bund**
- View skyline across the river in **Lujiazui**
- Optional rooftop drink or river cruise

**Food to try:** Xiaolongbao, shengjianbao, Shanghai-style noodles, braised pork.

---

# Day 7 — Shanghai highlights & depart

**Morning:**
- **Yu Garden** and old city area
- Try soup dumplings nearby

**Afternoon:**
Choose one based on your style:
- **Shanghai Museum** or **Urban Planning Exhibition Center**
- **Former French Concession**
- **Tianzifang**
- **Jing’an Temple**
- **Lujiazui** observation deck

**Evening:**
- Depart from Shanghai, or add an extra night if your flight leaves the next day.

---

## Suggested hotel areas

**Beijing:** Dongcheng, Wangfujing, Qianmen, Sanlitun  
**Xi’an:** Bell Tower, South Gate, Muslim Quarter area  
**Shanghai:** The Bund, People’s Square, Jing’an, Former French Concession

---

## Transport plan

- **Beijing → Xi’an:** High-speed train  
- **Xi’an → Shanghai:** Flight if short on time; train if you prefer rail  
- **Within cities:** Metro + DiDi/taxis  
- **Payments:** Set up **Alipay** and/or **WeChat Pay** before arrival if possible. Many places accept mobile payments more readily than foreign cards.

---

## Practical tips

- **Bring your passport daily** for trains, attraction tickets, and hotel check-in.
- **Book trains early**, especially around Chinese public holidays.
- Avoid traveling during **Chinese New Year** or **National Day Golden Week** if you dislike crowds.
- Use a VPN or roaming/eSIM if you need access to Western apps.
- Download offline Chinese in Google Translate or use Pleco.
- For maps, Apple Maps tends to work better in China than Google Maps.

---

## If you want a slower version

If you dislike moving cities quickly, do:

**Beijing 4 days → Shanghai 3 days**

You’d skip Xi’an, but the pace is easier:
- Beijing: Forbidden City, Great Wall, hutongs, Summer Palace
- Shanghai: Bund, French Concession, Yu Garden, Suzhou day trip

But for a first trip, I’d recommend the **Beijing–Xi’an–Shanghai** route above. It gives you the strongest mix of ancient, imperial, and modern China in one week.
